title: Shannon entropy
summary: H(X) = -Σ p(x) log2 p(x). Measures average information content in bits. Minimum bits to encode a random variable. Source coding theorem: can compress to H(X) bits per symbol (lossless) or H(X|Y) with side info.

ext.summary: H(X) = -Σ p(x) log2 p(x). Measures average information content in bits. Minimum bits to encode a random variable. Source coding theorem: can compress to H(X) bits per symbol (lossless) or H(X|Y) with side info.

structure.meaning: H(X) = -Σ p(x) log2 p(x). Uniform distribution maximizes entropy: H = log2(n) for n symbols.
H(X,Y) = -Σ p(x,y) log2 p(x,y). H(X,Y) ≤ H(X)+H(Y).
H(X|Y) = H(X,Y) - H(Y). Information X provides given Y.
I(X;Y) = H(X) - H(X|Y) = H(Y) - H(Y|X). Symmetric measure of dependence.
C = max I(X;Y) over input distributions. Shannon's channel coding theorem: can achieve any rate R < C with arbitrarily low error.

notes: Shannon's 1948 paper 'A Mathematical Theory of Communication' founded information theory.
Entropy is the fundamental limit of lossless compression.
Channel capacity is the fundamental limit of reliable communication.
Kolmogorov complexity K(x) = minimum program length to produce x. K(x) ≤ H(x) + O(1).
Mutual information is used in feature selection, clustering, and dependency analysis.
